text.p: Germany may have unearthed a new tennis star in 19-year-old Tommy Haas, who overcame his second seeded opponent in four days on Friday to reach the semifinals of the German Open.

Haas, who left school less than a year ago and entered the tournament as a wildcard, beat the 11th-seeded Spanish clay court expert Alberto Berasategui 2-6 6-3 6-3 to the delight of 12,000 local supporters in the Rothenbaum stadium.
On Wednesday, the 123rd-ranked Haas beat third-seeded Spaniard Carlos Moya, the Australian Open finalist, in straight sets and even Boris Becker has been impressed.

"He has the potential to get into the top 50 or even higher - very soon," said Becker, who has helped train Haas. The youngster now meets another Spaniard, Felix Mantilla, Becker's conqueror on Thursday.
Saturday's other semifinal will be between Yevgeny Kafelnikov, the second-seeded Russian, and the Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev, twice a former champion.

Medvedev, who is unseeded but beat Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek on Thursday, once more showed his liking for Hamburg by bringing down another seed, the 12th-ranked former French Open champion Sergei Bruguera.
He eventually triumphed 6-4 7-6 after enduring a delay of an hour for rain at set point at 40-30 in the 10th game.
Haas, based at Nick Bollettieri's tennis academy in Florida, played a remarkably mature match to overcome both his nerves and a fast-moving baseline opponent with a great deal of experience on clay.
"I was very, very nervous, as this was a new experience and I had no chance in the first set," said Haas.
"But it was great to have such support and when I felt more confidenied to give it all I had."

In the fifth game of the final set Haas produced, in successive rallies, a drop-shot winner from five feet behind the baseline, a backhand half-volley drop winner while attemptimg to serve and volley, and a forehand drop-shot which was angled so wide it opened up the court for an easy backhand pass.
Soon he was serving an ace to reach match point, and then fastened on to a net-cord which fell short to make a winning approach to the net.
Kafelnikov, meanwhile, scored a comfortable 6-3 6-0 win over Albert Costa, winning 6-3 6-0 in a contest which lasted less than an hour.
Afterwards the Russian pronounced himself pleased with the recovery of the broken finger which kept him out for three months this year.
"But I am better now, and winning today has made me as happy as when I was winning the French Open," said the 1996 Roland Garros champion.
